expectations.evidence: "A resistance factor is a deliberate discount applied to how strong we *think* a structure is, so the design still works when our estimate is a bit too optimistic." The answer keeps the safety meaning intact: "the margin that absorbs our ignorance" and "The worse our knowledge and the more abrupt the failure, the smaller the φ."

"\"Resistance factor\" and \"safety factor\" are not the same thing. A safety factor is one blanket number; φ is calibrated against statistics of real test data and target reliability. Also, φ is not a guarantee — it is a probabilistic bet, set by the code, not by the individual engineer."
